item.title: Trump Removes Sanctions on Russia to Help Oil Flow Amid Iran Conflict
item.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said it was “unfortunate” that the move could benefit Russia, but maintained that it was only for the short term.

item.title: Here’s What Happened in the War in the Middle East on Thursday
item.summary: Iran’s new supreme leader delivered a forceful message in his first public statement since succeeding his slain father, as the Israeli military bombarded Tehran and the Lebanese capital with strikes.

item.title: War in Iran Has India Scrambling to Keep Stoves Lit for Cooking
item.summary: India relies on huge quantities of cooking gas that is normally shipped from the Persian Gulf.

item.title: A Weakened Iran Hits Back by Strangling the Vital Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: The threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz are complicating President Trump’s calculations about how and when to end the war.

item.title: What Is the Strait of Hormuz and Why Is Iran Blocking It?
item.summary: With attacks and threats, Tehran is using the world’s most important transit point for oil and gas as leverage against its enemies.

item.title: New Iranian Leader Vows to Keep Global Oil Gateway Blocked
item.summary: Oil prices surged on Thursday after ships came under attack in the Persian Gulf, and Iran’s supreme leader vowed revenge for U.S. and Israeli airstrikes.

item.title: Iraq vents anger at strikes on former militias now under government control.
Yanar Mohammed, 65, Iraqi Women’s Rights Advocate, Is Killed by Gunmen
item.summary: She established a network of safe houses for abused women and was an outspoken critic of her country’s repressive institutions, despite the constant threat of violence.

item.title: Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran’s New Supreme Leader, Says Strait of Hormuz Must Remain Closed in Defiant Statement
item.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei struck a defiant tone and signaled that Iran would not back down in a war that has spread across the Middle East.

item.title: Displaced Lebanese Haunted by Strikes from the Sky
item.summary: With airstrikes expanding beyond the limits of Beirut’s southern suburbs, people in the city say that even the once-safest corners may no longer be off-limits.
